candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — cardiovascular drug interactions
candidate.educational_objective: Monitor for excessive bradycardia and AV conduction abnormalities when verapamil is combined with a beta blocker.

options.A: Marked tachycardia from additive sympathetic stimulation
options.B: Severe hypernatremia from renal sodium retention
options.C: Excessive bradycardia or atrioventricular conduction block from additive cardiac effects
options.D: Profound hyperglycemia from increased insulin resistance

candidate.rationale: Verapamil labeling warns that concomitant beta blockers can produce additive negative effects on heart rate and atrioventricular conduction, including excessive bradycardia and AV block.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Verapamil plus beta blockers can have additive effects on heart rate and AV conduction, causing excessive bradycardia or AV block.
candidate.source_locator: Drug Interactions — Beta-Blockers: additive negative effects on heart rate and AV conduction
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
candidate.stem: A client receives verapamil together with a beta blocker. Which adverse effect is most important for the nurse to monitor?
